evidence: src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts: `constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) {}` sets up an injected data-access dependency
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts: `log()` runs `const prisma = new PrismaClient(); await prisma.payrollAudit.create(...)` and never uses the injected `this.prisma`
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts: `trail()` uses `this.prisma.payrollAudit.findMany(...)`, so the same class has two different access paths

src/business/services/PayrollService.ts: the constructor injects `EmployeeRepository` and `TimesheetRepository`, and all data access goes through repository methods (`byId`, `create`, `approve`, `active`, `forWeek`)
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts builds the record id inline (`${Date.now()}-${subject}`) and talks directly to the raw Prisma model; it doesn't follow the module's repository pattern
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with payroll, so the concern is shared. The unit still fails because PayrollAuditService goes around its own injected abstraction. Its constructor takes a `PrismaService`, and `trail()` uses `this.prisma`. But `log()` ignores that dependency and creates `new PrismaClient()` on every call, so the two methods of one class reach the database in different ways. This also breaks consistency across the module. PayrollService reaches persistence only through its injected repositories (`EmployeeRepository`, `TimesheetRepository`). PayrollAuditService instead works directly against Prisma models (`payrollAudit.create` / `findMany`) and builds the record id inline. So the module has no single way of reaching data.

violations.message: `log()` creates a new `PrismaClient()` itself instead of using the injected `PrismaService` (`this.prisma`), which `trail()` does use. This goes around the class's own injected abstraction and leaves two different persistence paths in one service.

Uses raw Prisma model calls (`payrollAudit.create` / `findMany`) while the sibling `PayrollService` reaches data only through repository abstractions. The module's services don't share one abstraction for data access.
